name: El Salvador (14 stars, 1875–1912)
description: Nine alternating horizontal stripes of blue and white with a red canton bearing fourteen white five-pointed stars in rows of five, four and five.
history: Final version of the 1865 'conservative flag', with fourteen stars for the fourteen departments after Morazán was created in 1875. Because it resembled the flag of the United States too closely for the anti-imperialist mood of the time, the Legislative Assembly replaced it on 17 May 1912 with the blue-white-blue triband, first hoisted on 15 September 1912.
